full_judgment: 6. Mr. Mahbubey Alam, learned Senior Advocate appearing on behalf of the appellants made submissions in line with the grounds upon which leave was granted. He further submitted that the name of the predecessors of the plaintiffs having been recorded as korfa tenants and there being no materials on record to show that they were evicted from the suit land or they have surrendered their possession, the High Court Division committed an error in dismissing the suit without considering that after acquisition of the rent receiving interest the tenant acquired right in the suit land by operation of law. He further submitted that the trial Court as well as the Appellate Court having found the right and possession of the plaintiffs in the suit land, the High Court Division committed an error in dismissing the suit without reversing the finding of the court below and thus the same is not a proper judgment of reversal. He submitted that the plaintiffs are able to prove their title and possession over the suit land. The trial Court on a technical point dismissed the suit and the appellate Court being the Court of law and fact on elaborate discussion of evidence on record decreed the suit, but the High Court Division without reversing the finding and decision of the appellate Court as contemplated under Order XLI, rule 31 of the Code of Civil Procedure made the Rule absolute and as such the same is liable to be set aside.
